title: Delete unreachable storage entry points and never-used task states
outcome: Storage functions that nothing in production reaches are gone, thin wrappers kept only for tests are test-only, and the task lifecycle keeps only the state ever stored, while live turn-grant context assembly and task-change delivery behave exactly as before.
acceptance: Docs no longer describe removed entry points as available, and the doc link check passes
Live turn-grant context assembly and task-change delivery are unchanged, and their tests still pass
No table definition changes, and the new build passes readiness and doctor on a copy of each live store

Public storage functions with no production caller are out of the production build: record_turn_observation and explain_context are removed with the helpers only they used; task_delta, task_changes_since, search_memories, append_task_object, show_memory and rebuild_memory_index compile only for tests, which reach live logic through them
TaskState keeps only Active, the finalizer turn purpose stays a parseable host value that is always refused, and no stored record in either live store uses a removed state
Tests that exercised only removed code are deleted
Thin test-only wrappers over live code (build_context, start_task, join_task, bind_control_session and both checkpoint_control_turn convenience variants) compile only for tests

completion.summary: Unreachable storage entry points are out of the production build. record_turn_observation and explain_context are deleted; the remaining public wrappers reach live logic only from tests and compile only for tests. TaskState keeps only Active, and finalizer turns are always refused. Live turn-grant context assembly and task-change delivery are unchanged. The changes are committed as 1ad8b2b and pushed.
